question: Let $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix},\quad P=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&p\end{bmatrix},\quad Q=\begin{bmatrix}q&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}.$$ If $AP=I$ and $QA=I$, determine $p$ and $q$, and use the associative property of matrix multiplication to establish that $P=Q$ and hence that the inverse of $A$ is unique.
explanation:
Determination of $p$

From $AP=I$, $$\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&p\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&p-1\\0&2p-1\end{bmatrix}$$ Since this equals $I$, $$p-1=0,\quad 2p-1=1$$ Both conditions give $$p=1$$ Thus, $$P=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$$

Determination of $q$

From $QA=I$, $$\begin{bmatrix}q&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}q-1&q-2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$$ Hence, $$q-1=1,\quad q-2=0$$ giving $$q=2$$ Therefore, $$Q=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$$

Establishing Uniqueness

Using $AP=I$, $QA=I$ and associativity of matrix multiplication, $$P=IP=(QA)P=Q(AP)=QI=Q$$ Thus, $P=Q$. Since $AP=I$ and $P=Q$ together with $QA=I$ give both $AP=I$ and $PA=I$, the matrix $P$ is the inverse of $A$. Any left and right inverse obtained in this way must coincide. Therefore, the inverse is unique and $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$$.
